title: Streaming surface (SSE + A2UI)
description: What the gateway streams and what the web client renders (§12). This is the one interface the two share, so it lives in the contract rather than in either side.

RenderableComponent.title: RenderableComponent
RenderableComponent.description: The eight components from §12. Coverage, preference and readiness information are section/field variants of these — never a new component, and never a new UI system per feature.

instance_id.description: Stable for the life of the surface slot. Re-rendering the same instance id replaces it rather than adding a second one — which is what makes an SSE replay idempotent on the client (§12: re-rendering never creates a second booking).

props.description: Component-specific. Validated against the component's own schema before it reaches the client; the gateway never forwards an unvalidated agent payload (§2.1).

workflow_state_version.description: The version this instance was built from. A client action carrying a stale version is refused rather than applied (§9).

action.description: The server-validated action this component submits. Null for display-only components. The client never invents an action: it echoes one the server issued.

submitted.description: Set once the patient has answered this instance, so a replayed surface cannot solicit the same choice twice.

notice.description: Inline explanation, e.g. why an option is unavailable or that a value is unknown rather than absent (§2.2).

event_id.description: Content-addressed id used for SSE replay (§12) and for deduplicating authoritative events (§15). Replaying from a given id must reproduce the same sequence and must not create a second booking.

seq.description: Monotonic within a workflow. A client that sees a gap knows it missed an event and should replay.

type.title: StreamEventType
type.description: `partial_text` is explicitly NOT final state (§2.1: partial agent output is never committed). `terminal` closes the stream and carries the outcome; the client must not infer completion from the stream simply ending.

payload.description: Typed by `type`: a SurfaceUpdate for surface_update, a WorkflowStateChange for workflow_state, and so on.

progress_elapsed_ms.description: Progress latency, measured separately from final-response latency (§12). Null on a terminal event, which carries the final timing instead.

synthetic.description: True for fixture and offline-profile output, so the UI can label it and no admin chart can present canned data as a measurement (§12, §18).

components.description: Ordered. A later update replaces instances by `instance_id`; it never appends a duplicate.

remove_instance_ids.description: Instances the client must drop, so a superseded choice cannot be re-submitted.

degraded.description: Set when this step ran on a reduced pipeline (§10). Surfaced to the patient, because an unknown answer produced without the directory is a different answer.

command_id.description: The idempotency key for this action (§7). A resubmitted action reuses it, so a double-click or a retried request cannot become a second booking.

value.description: The patient's answer. Validated server-side against the component's schema; form data is never trusted because it came from the client (§6, §12).
